answer: Agents can earn reputation only through escrowed exchanges with counterparties whose own histories predate the trade; a new identity gets no credit merely for appearing in a pearl inlet of accounts. Each completed deal locks a small stake until both sides confirm delivery, and disputes can slash it. Splitting into sybils therefore does not multiply trust: the attacker must fund each account, sustain real trades with established agents, and risk repeated losses, pushing the cost of fake credibility toward its nadir only after costly proof.
